summary: Elizabeth Jane Oswald, a Scottish traveller who read the Icelandic sagas, made three summer journeys in Iceland, in 1875, 1878, and 1879, riding with companions and Icelandic guides on ponies and staying at farms and parsonages. She went from Reykjavik to Geysir, Thingvellir, and the sulphur mines of Krisuvik, round Hecla and across the Markarfljot to Njal’s country, through Borgarfjord and Hvalfjord, and on the third journey by the Faröe Islands to Akureyrei in the north and over the heaths to Vatzdale and back. Throughout she connects the places with the sagas and legends set in them, and two chapters are an account of Icelandic literature. She also writes about fishing, farming, housekeeping, church services, and recent hardships, with hints to travellers and translations of verse. Woodcuts after her own sketches and a map of the saga districts.
notes_on_text: The book prints the Icelandic letters thorn and eth as “th” and “d” (its Note says so); that is kept.
The printed errata slip (four items) has been applied.

The map is printed across two pages; a narrow strip of it is lost in the binding of the scanned copy, so it is shown in two halves. The letters lost from its title (“al” of “Local”, “Ce” of “Certain”) are supplied.
